extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers and policymakers interested in U.S. economic policy
extracted.subtask_description: Summarizing and reporting President Truman's midyear economic report to Congress, including its diagnoses of economic risks and recommended policy actions for government, business, labor and the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strengthen defenses against inflation
rubrics_metrics.description: The nation must strengthen its defenses against inflation; inflationary problems may become stronger.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mr. Truman warned inflationary pressures could grow and that adjustments must be made before lack of them produces serious unemployment and business decline. Price stability and timely adjustments are necessary to prevent a price-wage spiral.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full publicity on farm outlook
rubrics_metrics.description: Full publicity as to the true farm outlook, perhaps including a campaign for 'strict ... in the use of some foods.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep the public informed of agricultural facts so unfounded rumors do not lead to speculation, hoarding and unnecessary buying; transparency to prevent market panic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quick planning for conservation and export controls
rubrics_metrics.description: Quick planning for conservation through export controls and possibly by renewing the Government's recently lapsed power to control the amount of grain used by distillers and other processors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a serious crop shortage develops, plans should be readied well in advance to conserve supplies and ensure wise usage; government may restore specific restrictions if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industries should forgo immediate price increases
rubrics_metrics.description: Coal, steel and other industries should forgo immediate price increases until they test the real costs of wage increases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mr. Truman urged industries not to raise prices hastily based on expectations or speculation; increases based on exaggerated interpretation could start another price-wage spiral.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stability in steel prices
rubrics_metrics.description: Stability in steel prices would be a wise economic policy for this year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because increases in steel would have a widespread inflationary effect, steel companies should exercise extraordinary caution and offset cost increases through efficiency and savings rather than raising prices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Price reductions where profit margins permit
rubrics_metrics.description: Businesses with adequate profits should permit price reductions or absorb wage increases when profit margins allow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Price cuts and adjustments remain needed in many cases to check declines in demand and provide outlets for increased production; recent favorable earnings should permit absorption of extraordinary costs short-term to stabilize prosperity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare to lower consumer prices where justified
rubrics_metrics.description: Where future profits would be better protected by assuring larger volume through lower prices, businesses should make these adjustments now.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lowering prices can increase volume and protect long-term profits; avoid pyramiding of wage-price increases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep wage increases tied to productivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Except for special circumstances, wage increases should be related to general trends in productivity and not made on a basis which forces price increases or prevents price reductions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wage rises are still needed in some areas to alleviate hardship, but broad wage demands should correspond to productivity to avoid inflationary pressure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not use coal settlement as a universal precedent
rubrics_metrics.description: The coal contract does not provide a guide or pattern for wage settlements in other fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The coal wage reflects the character and labor needs of that industry; other industries governed by different circumstances should not base their demands on the coal settlement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absorb coal cost increases via productivity and profit margins
rubrics_metrics.description: Efforts should be made to absorb cost increases in the coal mining industry and indirectly affected industries through increased productivity and reduction in profit margins.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pyramiding of price advances by coal distributors is unjustified; operating adjustments toward maximum efficiency should help restore lower coal prices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise caution on distributor price pyramiding
rubrics_metrics.description: Pyramiding of price advances by distributors is wholly unjustified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distributors should not multiply price increases up the chain; cost increases should be absorbed where possible rather than passed through repeatedly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Housing: enact comprehensive housing program and continue rent controls
rubrics_metrics.description: Immediate enactment of the comprehensive housing program previously recommended to Congress, and continuance of rent controls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction and housing are the domestic problem No. 1; housing costs can and should be substantially lowered through efforts of material suppliers, builders and workers. Without such law, housing is seriously handicapped.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lower housing and construction costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Housing and other construction costs should be held to moderate amounts consistent with essential needs, and materially lowered by suppliers, builders and workers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A much higher volume of housing output is needed to sustain maximum employment when temporary sustaining forces decline; lowering construction costs is essential to increase output.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increase the minimum wage and extend coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Increase the minimum wage from 40 to 65 cents an hour, with coverage extended to farm and other workers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This legislative action, together with enlarged social-security benefits, is urged to help those whose incomes remain substandard and to adjust to higher cost of living.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enlarge social-security benefit payments
rubrics_metrics.description: Increase old-age pensions and other social-security benefits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required to account for the higher cost of living and to support those with substandard incomes; part of legislative responsibilities of government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign aid objective: restore stable world economy
rubrics_metrics.description: The immediate and sole objective of our foreign aid programs should be to restore a vigorous, stable, and peaceful world economy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foreign aid should enable other countries to pay their way by mutual exchange of goods and services; aid is not to be used to support maximum domestic production and employment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appraise export impacts on domestic economy
rubrics_metrics.description: Carefully appraise the impact of exports on the domestic economy, especially when large excesses of exports over imports create domestic strain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exports supporting foreign rehabilitation have produced some domestic shortages; exports are temporary props and may decline, so policy must consider domestic effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep preparedness for possible crop shortages
rubrics_metrics.description: Two lines of action: (1) keep the public informed of agricultural outlook at all times to avoid speculation and hoarding; (2) have conservation plans ready well in advance if situation becomes serious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No immediate suggestion for consumer rationing but government should seek voluntary cooperation of grain trade and consider restoring restrictions on grain use by processors if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid immediate tax reductions
rubrics_metrics.description: Against tax cuts now — tax reduction would add to inflationary pressures and prevent the debt reduction which should be carried out in prosperous times.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A policy of fiscal restraint now will enable the government to have tools available if intervention is later needed; maintain sound financial policies and debt reduction in prosperous times.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make timely adjustments before crisis
rubrics_metrics.description: Adjustments must be made before the lack of them produces serious unemployment and business decline; waiting until bad results appear means action is too late.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moderate measures in time can accomplish more than drastic delay or neglect; adjustments take time and should be proactive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government responsibilities for legislative and long-range programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Legislative action on minimum wages, social security and housing; long-range programs for resource and regional development, health and welfare, anti-monopoly programs, stabilization devices and other undertakings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Government must provide complementary influence and enact necessary laws to sustain long-term stable prosperity; studies are under way to prepare these for presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bring prices and wages in line with productivity via collective bargaining
rubrics_metrics.description: It is in the interest of steady expansion that, with the aid of collective bargaining, prices and wages be brought in line with general productivity trends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This alignment helps avoid inflationary mismatches and supports stable long-term employment and production.
